title: What an owner's browser gets in the admin
grade_reasons: D, on the build's own figures, recomputed here from route-bundle-stats.json. Every signed-in screen loads about twice the script it needs (median 1,152,953 bytes where about 650,000 will do; 481 KB of it is three stray imports), 27 screens load an editor or a catalogue they never draw (up to 4.27 MB), a product editor's document is two thirds words that no part reads, and each screen makes 23 to 46 background requests. Budgets watch 9 of 449 routes and none of the worst four, and no document or request count is held. The base is better than the letter says: the heavy libraries already load on demand and the seven most-used screens are held from growing, which is why most of the fix is small.

measures.name: First scripts of a plain signed-in screen
measures.today: Median of the 449 admin routes: 1,152,953 bytes raw. The store home: 1,194,862 raw / 360,861 gzip. 337 of 449 routes sit between 1.0 and 1.3 MB. Source: .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json, recomputed by the steward. 481 KB of every screen is Supabase's client, zod and the page builder's English, on 420 to 432 routes.
measures.target_a: Median at or under 650,000 bytes raw. The store home, orders, products, settings and the platform home each at or under 680,000 (about 210 KB gzip).
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs over .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json after each build (created by the work item 'One check over every route'), and the seven screens of e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is about 511 KB and cannot go: 447,102 bytes of React and Next that all 560 routes share (133,758 gzip), and about 64 KB for the admin's frame (menus, rail, tooltips, the AI manager's launcher). 650,000 leaves a screen about 140 KB for its own code. The findings' own bars are 700,000 to 760,000 for the home; that is a B. The simulation on the built chunks gives a median near 634,000, so the bar can be met with about 2% to spare.

measures.name: Script a plain screen has loaded by the time it is idle
measures.today: 1,428,740 bytes on the store home (m/loaded.json, local build): 1,187,034 in the first load and 241,706 after it. Nothing budgets the second part: the spec reads the HTML's script tags only. On the local build most of the after-load part is the storefront's scripts, pulled by the View store link.
measures.target_a: At or under 800,000 bytes raw five seconds after load, with Supabase's realtime, storage and database clients in none of it.
measures.how_measured: A new case in e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts that sums every script response until the page is idle (created by the gap item 'Session without the whole Supabase client'). It is steady only once nothing is prefetched at rest.
measures.why_this_is_a: The planned cut moves Supabase's client (259,469 bytes with realtime and a Buffer polyfill) from the first load to after idle. It does not remove it, so a first-load budget alone would call a screen of about 930 KB done. The need is one token refresh; the auth client alone is about 117 KB as built. 800,000 is the first-load bar plus that. A B accepts bytes that only moved.

measures.name: The page builder's first scripts, and the ceiling for every other route
measures.today: Builder: 3,303,372 bytes raw / 1,014,731 gzip on a store's editor routes. 39 routes carry the builder's chunk: 26 editors and 13 previews that draw no editor. 90 routes are over 1.3 MB and 40 over 3 MB. The largest is 4,274,839 (a Work invoice).
measures.target_a: The builder at or under 1,800,000 bytes raw (about 555 KB gzip), with the rich text editor and the store's language arriving after first paint. No other route over 1,300,000. At most 26 routes over that line, each named in the baseline.
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs: a ceiling per kind of route (builder, anything else) and the count of routes over 1.3 MB, read from route-bundle-stats.json.
measures.why_this_is_a: Floor, an estimate from the built chunks: React and Next 447 KB, the frame 64 KB, zod 117 KB (the builder checks the page model as you type), and about 1.0 MB for the canvas, the page model and the store's own block views: about 1.6 MB. What need not come first: the rich text editor 435 KB, four store languages 368 KB, Supabase 259 KB, English copies about 150 KB, and about 300 KB of dialogs and of field forms for the 37 block types. The findings' own bar is 2,450,000; that is a B. 1.8 MB is the floor plus about 12%.

measures.name: Code a screen downloads for something it does not draw
measures.today: First-load chunks by marker: Supabase's client on 432 of 449 routes, zod on 432, the builder's English on 423, the rich text editor on 73 (34 outside the builder's family), a whole storefront language on 40. 13 previews load the whole builder (3.2 to 3.3 MB). One first-load chunk is 1,704,595 bytes. The AI manager's chat is 496,206 bytes on its first opening, about 95% of it three tables read for two labels.
measures.target_a: Supabase on 0 routes. The rich text editor on 0. A whole storefront language on 0. Any English catalogue but common and sign-in on 0. zod on at most 160 routes, a list that may only shrink. No first-load chunk over 600,000 bytes. The chat's scripts on first opening at or under 130,000.
measures.how_measured: Marker strings searched in each route's first-load chunks by scripts/bundle-budget.mjs; src/components/admin/admin-bundle.scan.test.ts with its starting lists empty; e2e/signed-in/ai-manager-panel.spec.ts for the chat.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is zero: none of these is needed to paint the screens that carry them. Stated tolerance: zod (116,870 raw, 32,996 gzip) stays on screens whose own forms check input in the browser, and the rich text editor's 435 KB arrives in the builder after first paint. The chat's own code is 39 files and 302,869 bytes of source; 130,000 built is that plus about 10%. A B leaves today's offenders on lists that 'may only shrink'; an A has the lists empty.

measures.name: Words in a document that no part of the page reads
measures.today: Every store screen is handed 34.0 KB of words and reads about 12 KB; the setup area (6.9 KB) has no reader at all. The product editor is handed 238.5 KB and reads 78.9 KB. The builder is handed 311.6 KB and reads 195.4 KB. Words are 63% of the payload over 16 admin documents (1,227 of 1,943 KB). Documents: store home 165,942 characters, product editor 426,497 bytes (108 KB gzip), builder 585,943 (136 KB gzip).
measures.target_a: Unread words at or under 10% of the words handed, on each budgeted screen. Documents: store home at or under 140,000, product editor at or under 290,000, builder at or under 480,000.
measures.how_measured: Document budgets in e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts (added by 'One check over every route', lowered by the words item); admin-cuts.scan.test.ts keeps a reader from going back to a whole area; docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs draws the table.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is the markup and its twin as data, which React needs to wake the page, plus the words the parts on the page read. Tolerance: 10% for unread leaves of a group that is handed whole, and the builder's 195 KB of read words travelling in each document (moving them into a cached script is a trial with a known risk, D540). A B keeps whole areas and budgets today's size.

measures.name: Requests an idle admin screen makes
measures.today: 23 to 46 router prefetches per screen (home 28 for 13 links, 98 KB on the wire; pages list 46), and about 25 again after every refresh or save. One notice poll per load and every 60 seconds per visible tab: 60 requests and 240 statements an hour.
measures.target_a: 0 router prefetches in the 3 seconds after load and at most 2 after pointing at a link. At most 6 poll requests an hour from an untouched tab, each at most 2 statements after the account read.
measures.how_measured: e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts (created by the prefetch item); a signed-in spec with a clock and assistant-notices.int.test.ts (created by the notice item).
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is zero prefetches: what the admin fetches ahead is a loading skeleton, nearly the same for every route, and pointing at a link fetches it in time. The poll's floor is one cheap count while the person is there. A B would cap today's counts; an A asks for nothing nobody pointed at.

measures.name: What grows with the catalogue: bytes per row on a list
measures.today: The Products list sends every product of the store: about 0.9 KB of document per product, no limit in the read (src/server/products.ts, listAdminProducts). An estimated 4.5 MB at 5,000 products. The test stores have 10, so nothing shows today.
measures.target_a: At most 100 rows a page: a store with 500 products gets a Products document under 300,000 characters that says '100 of 500'.
measures.how_measured: A seeded case created by the Products item. The admin-data area holds the other lists the same way (AD-10).
measures.why_this_is_a: A list must not grow in a straight line with the store. 100 rows is what the storefront's listings and code review step 1.13 already use. There is no B here: a list is bounded or it is not.

measures.name: What holds it: routes under a budget, and the speed owners get
measures.today: 9 of 449 admin routes have a script budget. No document and no request count has one. The import walk covers shoppers' code only. The one production figure, the admin's own speed beacon, read 3.93 s LCP at p75 over 52 loads on 31 October (INP 136 ms), before 1.1 MB left each screen. It has not been read since, and nothing warns when it is not good.
measures.target_a: 449 of 449 routes in a baseline that only falls (15,000 bytes of room a route). Document and request budgets on the store home, orders, a product's editor and the builder. The import walk green with empty lists. LCP at p75 at or under 2.5 s and INP at or under 200 ms for every kind of admin screen with 100 loads or more in 28 days, with a line in the platform's briefing when one is not.
measures.how_measured: scripts/bundle-budget.mjs in CI; e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts and prefetch.spec.ts; admin-bundle.scan.test.ts; Platform, Usage and limits (commerce.own_speed_samples, site 'admin') and the briefing line the gap item adds.
measures.why_this_is_a: An A needs every measure held by a test or a production figure. Bytes are a stand-in; the beacon is what owners feel, and 2.5 s and 200 ms are Google's 'good', the line the storefront is already held to. A B has budgets on scripts only and reads the field figure when someone remembers.

tolerated.why: 40% of the built client files are second copies of modules, but a browser meets about 14% of that while moving around the admin, and it is the chunker working as designed. Measure again after them, and adopt the flag only if a 59-screen tour falls by 10% or more with no budget raised.

gaps.title: After the cuts, 259 KB of Supabase still loads on every screen once it is idle, and no budget counts script fetched after the HTML's own
gaps.evidence: Opened: src/components/admin/session.tsx lines 8 and 22. SessionKeeper calls createClient().auth.onAuthStateChange() to keep the token fresh, and src/lib/supabase/client.ts builds the whole client (createBrowserClient of @supabase/ssr). In the built chunks of the admin home (m/loaded.json) the auth client is 103,361 bytes; realtime with phoenix 57,224, storage 23,172, the database client 17,166 and a 22,750-byte Buffer polyfill ride with it, and the browser ran 22,809 of the main chunk's 179,419 bytes and 6,770 of realtime's 57,349. AC-1 and BN-1 move the import to idle and both note that the bytes stay. docs/rules/admin/platform.md lines 50-51 says tokens are refreshed in the browser. e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts lines 18-23 sums the HTML's script tags only, so bytes that move to after load leave every budget.
gaps.proposed_work_item: Session without the whole Supabase client, and a by-idle budget. Try two ways and keep one: the auth client alone with the same cookie storage (about 117 KB as built), or a small refresh route called before the token expires (0 KB; it changes the rule in platform.md and how two tabs share a refresh token). Uploads keep importing the full client on the press. Add a case to admin-scripts.spec.ts that sums every script response until the page is idle. Done when an idle store home has loaded at or under 800,000 bytes of script (1,428,740 today; about 930,000 after the planned cuts) and none of it is Supabase's realtime, storage or database client. Phase next, effort M, after the frame cut and the prefetch item.
